## 伊朗協議露曙光，美債全面上漲

美國總統取消原定攻擊，並表示可能宣布與伊朗達成協議，美債週四大幅上漲。油價下跌，使市場完全反映 Fed 升息的時間，由 12 月延至 2027 年第一季。10 年期殖利率下降 10 個基點至 4.45%，實質殖利率與通膨補償各貢獻一半降幅。

與週三核心 CPI 較溫和卻未能帶動持續漲勢不同，這次緩解擴及各市場。半導體大漲 7.91%，高收益債上漲，波動率下降。投資人看好能源風險減輕後的成長與通膨組合，而非因成長疲弱逃向安全資產。30 年期美債殖利率重返 5% 以下，增額標售投標倍數改善，直接投標人參與也高。

經濟與政策消息仍有需要保留的部分。生產者物價漲幅超出預期，且不限於能源，初領失業金則增加；ECB 升息，並保留再次行動的空間。信用市場中，Citi 與 CoreWeave 完成大型發行，Hanuman Wind Power 卻即使提供高殖利率，仍再度延後首次發債。油價降低共同壓力，沒有消除借款人體質差異，也沒有抹去已傳入供應鏈的通膨。

## 油價緩解壓過偏熱的生產者物價

協議預期降低戰爭溢價，WTI 下跌 2.58% 至 $87.71，布蘭特下跌 2.92% 至 $90.38。地緣消息前，市場完全反映 Fed 在 12 月前升息 25 個基點；收盤時，這個時點已移至 2027 年第一季。升息風險被往後推，而不是轉成降息預期。

美債各天期同步上漲。2 年期殖利率下跌 8 個基點至 4.05%，5 年期下跌 9 個基點至 4.18%，30 年期下跌 8 個基點至 4.95%。2s10s 縮窄 2 個基點至 40 個基點，2s30s 維持 90 個基點；2s5s10s 蝶式利差維持 −14 個基點，2s10s30s 則因 10 年期領漲，下跌 4 個基點至 −10 個基點。

10 年期實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率各降 5 個基點，分別至 2.16% 與 2.29%。5 年期實質殖利率也下跌 5 個基點至 1.78%，7 年期下跌 6 個基點至 1.96%，20 年與 30 年期分別下跌 5 與 6 個基點至 2.53% 與 2.72%。通膨補償下降反映油價緩解，實質利率回落則伴隨近期緊縮迫切性降低。

這波漲勢回吐了不少近期升幅。2 年與 5 年期殖利率一週持平，但仍比一個月前高 10 與 11 個基點；10 年期一週下跌 2 個基點、一個月上升 3 個基點，30 年期則分別下跌 2 與 3 個基點。對政策較敏感的殖利率，仍高於 Fed 目標區間。

5 月 PPI 卻不令人放心。最終需求物價月增 1.1%，高於預估的 0.7%，年增 6.5%；排除食品、能源與貿易服務後，月增 0.8%、年增 5.1%，高於 0.5% 的月增預估。商品價格上漲 2.8%，其中能源大漲 10.7%，服務上漲 0.3%。壓力並非只來自原油。

失業金數據提供另一面。6 月 6 日當週初領增加 4,000 人至 22.9 萬，高於預估的 22 萬，四週平均升至 21.9 萬；5 月 30 日當週續領增加 2.4 萬至 179.5 萬。受保失業率維持 1.2%，但開始申領與持續領取給付的人數都增加。加上油價較低，Fed 在 6 月 16–17 日會議前選擇等待的代價有所下降。

風險資產也受惠於這種緩解。S&P 500 上漲 1.75%，Nasdaq 100 上漲 3.29%，半導體上漲 7.91%，VIX 下跌 12.51% 至 19.44。美元指數下跌 0.09% 至 99.86，黃金下跌 0.44% 至 $4,090.30。不過，戰爭期間談判消息已多次變化，而 PPI 顯示先前能源成本正在擴散。

## 標售順利，Fed 持續支撐準備金

$220 億 30 年期增額標售以 5.020% 得標，投標倍數由前次較大規模發行的 2.30 升至 2.33。間接投標人取得 59.95%，直接投標人 25.31%，交易商 14.74%。票息 5%、2056 年 5 月到期的債券，將在 6 月 15 日交割。較小供給由最終投資人承接，直接投標比重高，並未打斷當日漲勢。

國庫券需求較分歧。4 週券標售 $700 億，最高得標利率 3.595%，投標倍數由 3.07 升至 3.13，間接投標人取得 70.59%。$750.01 億 8 週券以 3.610% 得標，投標倍數由 3.20 降至 2.94，間接投標人取得 69.59%。兩者在 6 月 16 日交割；較短券種受惠於減量，8 週供給不變，投標倍數卻下降。

債券等值殖利率方面，4 週維持 3.67%，6 週維持 3.68%，8 週上升 1 個基點至 3.69%；13、17 與 26 週各下跌 1 個基點至 3.71%、3.76% 與 3.80%。52 週下跌 5 個基點至 3.85%，呼應升息時點後移。

Fed 將截至 7 月 13 日月度期間的國庫券購買計畫維持在約 $100 億，並安排約 $165 億再投資。截至 6 月 10 日一週，銀行準備金增加 $658 億至 $3.111 兆。財政部日後將現金餘額重建至 $1 兆以上時，原本會抽走銀行準備金，這些管理操作有助維持充裕流動性。

投資人也在評估主席 Kevin Warsh 將如何溝通政策。Pimco 顧問提到他先前對前瞻指引的批評，市場則討論較短的 FOMC 聲明、降低點陣圖重要性，以及減少主席記者會。這些變動都尚未採行。指引若減少，後續數據可能更能左右價格、事件波動可能增加，但這本身不代表利率或資產負債表政策改變。

## 信用市場獎勵清楚的融資計畫，卻非所有借款人

信用債 ETF 隨美債與股市上漲，LQD 上漲 0.85%、HYG 上漲 0.59%、JNK 上漲 0.57%。Citi 營運銀行完成今年首次同類發行，四批次共 $62.5 億，天期介於 2 至 6 年。最長券種從初步約美債加 95 個基點，收窄至 67 個基點，預期評等 Aa3、A+ 與 AA−，所得用於一般公司用途。

長期債務規定放寬，降低了 Citi 發行的迫切性。其他五大華爾街銀行今年已發行逾 $1,200 億，其中第一季超過 $650 億、創下紀錄。Citi 是週四三家投資等級發行人之一，當日總供給超過 $100 億。選擇在營運銀行而非控股公司發行，增加了較長期資金，並非為修補困境資產負債表。

Oracle 融資指引帶來可觀察的信用反應。至中午，3.65% 票息、2041 年到期券利差收窄 15 個基點至 2 個百分點；6.9% 票息、2052 年到期券收窄 12 個基點至 2.09 個百分點。五年期 CDS 最多下降 0.034 個百分點至 1.557。公司表示，預期曆年內不再發債，本會計年度計畫以 $400 億債務與股權融資支應，其中包括先前宣布的 $200 億按市價增發股票。

投資人獎勵的是資金安排更清楚，而非投資需求降低。全年資本支出已達 $557 億，高於 $500 億計畫，新年度淨支出預計約 $700 億。客戶預付款與提供運算設備，可減少眼前現金需求，但 Oracle 仍以約 $1,170 億債券，居美國投資等級指數最大非金融發行人。債券改善之際，股權投資人仍質疑龐大支出的報酬。

CoreWeave 則將先前行銷轉為完成的跨境發行：€20 億 6 年期票據殖利率 8.5%，$12.5 億 6 年期美元券殖利率 9.625%。歐元訂單超過 €70 億，涵蓋多數大型歐洲高收益債買家。Ba3/B+/BB− 評等、約 $350 億投資與 $260 億現金消耗預估，仍使槓桿與獲利不確定性需要高額補償，即使訂單強勁。

出租人的融資則呈現租戶風險如何傳遞。先前報導的 Applied Digital $15.9 億計畫，以 7% 融資、低於前一階段的 10%，但仍比近期 Amazon 相關計畫高近 1 個百分點。CoreWeave 五年期保障成本由 12 月的 8.81 個百分點降至 4.52 個百分點，幫助開發商為相關計畫籌得逾 $80 億。信用改善降低整條融資鏈成本，仍未抹去與大型雲端業者支持的差距。

參議員 Elizabeth Warren 提議，要求金融機構向金融研究辦公室申報 AI 債務與股權曝險，涵蓋晶片、資料中心、雲端與大型雲端業者，並列明工具、金額、交易對手、利率、條件、擔保品與表外債務。提案尚未成為法律。另一邊，SpaceX 向 IPO 投資人表示已取得三家機構的投資等級評等安排，此前 $200 億融資已降低市場隱含資金成本。$750 億股權籌資與後續發債預期，可能讓過橋融資轉成更大型的投資等級信用曝險。

Oaktree 為弱勢信用的再融資問題提供了規模估計：逾 $2,000 億高收益債與槓桿貸款，價格低於 90 美分、到期殖利率高於 15%，許多與 2021–2022 年收購案有關。利息計入本金與負債管理交易延後付款及到期日，但約三分之一、在 2028 年有債務到期的科技借款人，多年未證明可進入資本市場，預期將在下半年開始嘗試再融資，包括民間信貸中的企業軟體公司。

先前報導 CCC 相對較高品質高收益債約 6.4 個百分點的溢價、創 14 個月高點，如今有了具體到期案例。穆迪將 Travelodge 進一步調降至更低投機等級，€2.5 億 2030 年浮息券有 23% 借給放空者，2028 年券空單比重近 7%。公司未償票據約 £6.23 億，包括 2028 年 4 月到期的 £4.15 億擔保債。自由現金流為負、去槓桿有限，使再融資愈來愈難，與整體高收益債報酬強勁形成反差。

Hanuman Wind Power 則未能完成融資。Energy Absolute 子公司在延長收單一天後，第二次推遲國際高收益債首發。9% 中後段的殖利率，仍不足以克服對泰國母公司治理、過往詐欺指控及部分所得將轉給母公司的疑慮。15 年期美債利率上升，也降低擬議 15 年期、前五年不可贖回結構的相對吸引力。治理與現金流歸屬不清楚時，單靠高殖利率仍難說服買家。

## ECB 升息，歐洲債券仍維持漲勢

ECB 將存款利率提高 25 個基點至 2.25%，為近三年首次升息，也是首個因戰爭通膨衝擊採取行動的主要經濟體。Christine Lagarde 指出，能源正擴散至間接成本與預期。活動雖然放慢，尤其服務業，但她認為經濟仍能承受緊縮。

歐洲債券在決策後維持漲勢，10 年期殖利率下降 3 個基點至 3.05%，歐元約為 $1.1538。升息早已廣受預期；ECB 預測仍顯示通膨到 2027 年上半年高於目標，官員也不排除 7 月再升息，但 9 月仍是較普遍看法。投資人反映 2.25% 之後還有兩次升息。

IMF 假設 2026 年累計緊縮 50 個基點，將歐元區通膨預測由 2.4% 上修至 2.8%，成長由 1.1% 下修至 0.9%。較低油價有幫助，但官員仍擔心，即使達成和平協議，薪資、服務與預期仍可能保留先前衝擊的影響。

土耳其正式維持利率，一週附買回為 37%，已成主要融資管道的隔夜放款為 40%。年通膨連續兩個月加快至 32.6%，不過 5 月季調通膨略有改善，央行並收緊信貸成長限制。年底市場預期接近 30%，仍高於官方的 26%，第三季可能寬鬆需以通膨重新下降、里拉穩定為前提。

挪威調查支持更多耐心。挪威央行預估第二季產出成長 0.2%、第三季 0.3%，低於先前第二季 0.4% 的看法。招聘困難與產能限制減輕，降低 6 月再次升息壓力，即使核心通膨加快。薪資預期升至 4.5%，石油收入則支撐克朗。維持利率的理由是景氣較弱與貨幣較強，而非沒有物價壓力。

泰國則有不同的曲線機會。2s10s 接近 110 個基點，為 2022 年 11 月以來接近最陡水準，10 年期殖利率估計比合理價值高約 40 個基點。5 月通膨較溫和、成長偏弱，降低未來三至六個月升息的可能。若通膨維持受控、供給不壓過需求，長債可提供息收與沿曲線縮短天期的收益。

英國投資人在 6 月 18 日 Makerfield 補選與英格蘭銀行決策前，面對政治及財政不確定性。工黨領導地位可能遭挑戰，借款計畫因而可能改變，而 4 月赤字已創該月份六年高點。一般公債規模約 £2.1 兆，加上指數連結債與國庫券約 £2.9 兆；國家債務預估占 GDP 比率由 2023 年 98.8%，升至 2027 年 105.4%。財政方向一旦變化，長端尤其敏感。

## 全球情勢改善，印尼仍落後

美債殖利率與油價下降、美元略弱，改善共同環境，EMB 上漲 0.96%。印尼卻反向走弱，10 年期本幣殖利率上升 10 個基點至 7.45%，接近 2022 年以來最高；印尼盾下跌 0.2%，年內約貶 7%。外資撤出債市達 $5.97 億、股市 $39 億，分析師預期再緊縮 25–50 個基點，央行則容許更高殖利率以防衛匯率。

Danantara 仍完成首次美元發行，主權財富基金透過等額 5 年與 10 年券籌得 $15 億，5 年期殖利率 5.35%。兩批均比初步指引收窄約 35 個基點，但最終訂單不到兩倍，低於近期亞洲交易常見的三倍以上。基金也繼續考慮低於市場利率的本幣債。海外完成發行解決了一項需求，尚未解決本地信心與近期印尼美元債利差擴大的問題。

阿根廷前一晚升評則反映在交易價格。2035 年全球債最多上漲 2.9 美分至紀錄高點 79.4，2030 年券上漲逾 1.2 美分。S&P 由 CCC+ 升至 B−，建立在財政盈餘、逾 $100 億準備買進與外部流動性改善上。投資人認為利差有機會向 400–450 個基點收斂，可能重新打開國際發行管道，但信用仍屬投機等級。

尚比亞本幣債漲勢，結合投資管道改善與外債管理。2026 年本幣債報酬達 39%，超過第二名新興市場兩倍，受到殖利率下跌 120 個基點與克瓦查升值 24% 支撐。外資初級市場上限由 5% 提高至 23%，吸引流入，較強銅收入也有幫助；$13.6 億美元債買回預期可為電網釋出約 $2.75 億。這些變化共同支撐本地表現，並不表示漲勢完全由買回案造成。

Dangote 奈及利亞煉油廠準備 IPO、擴大這座對國內燃料供應重要的工廠，同時尋求最高 $10 億私募債務。投資人會議仍在進行，融資尚未完成；另一筆私募股權已吸引最高 $20 億意向需求，集團目標五年內投資至少 $400 億。最終槓桿、擔保品與幣別條件，將決定工業集團本身承擔多少風險，而非轉由銀行或國家承受。

委內瑞拉擬議顧問委任，呈現重整前的成本。與 Centerview 討論的草案，成功費為重整債務的 0.1%、不設金額上限；估計債權 $1,500 億至 $2,000 億，意味約 $1.5 億至 $2 億，另加每月 $75 萬及費用。工作涵蓋經濟分析、債權人策略與多邊協調，尚無最終契約或債務條件，債權範圍與專業成本仍待釐清。

辛巴威討論非洲開發銀行 $1.5 億貸款，作為籌集 $25 億清償積欠款項的一部分。國家自 1999 年被排除在國際資本市場外，希望重整約 $230 億債務。IMF 工作人員監督計畫與先前 AfDB $400 萬補助，改善了制度上的路徑；但過橋資金仍須促成與債權人的正常化，才有機會恢復一般發行。

秘魯第九個月維持利率 4.25%，利馬通膨由 4.01% 降至 3.91%，為 10 月以來首次月度放緩。能源、天然氣與食品衝擊後，通膨仍高於 1%–3% 目標。總統選票差距極小、計票仍使政治風險持續，但央行選擇等待供給壓力消退，而非立即升息。

## 後續數據檢驗升息延後的判斷

密西根大學初值調查在 6 月 12 日美東 10:00 公布，工業生產接續於 15 日 09:15。進出口物價與新屋開工在 16 日 08:30，零售銷售在 17 日 08:30，當日 14:00 是 FOMC 決策。通膨預期與利率敏感活動若轉弱，有利於維持 3.50%–3.75% 而不預告近期升息；價格再強、需求仍穩，則會在 Warsh 首次政策溝通前挑戰這波緩解。

6 月 15 日有 $1,190 億附息債總額交割，以及 $890 億 13 週、$770 億 26 週券標售；16 日有 $650 億 6 週券與 $130 億 20 年期增額發行，18 日則有 $240 億 5 年期 TIPS 增額發行。資金利率、配售結構、20 年期相對發行前交易的得標水準，以及實質殖利率需求，將呈現週四上漲後市場能否承接這些安排。

日銀與澳洲央行在 6 月 16 日決策，18 日接著是印尼、瑞士、挪威、英國及菲律賓央行。日銀預期將利率提高至接近 1%；其他焦點是維持利率的央行是否仍保留緊縮語氣，以及印尼或菲律賓是否為防衛匯率、因應進口通膨而升息。油價較低增加政策分歧空間，匯率再弱或長債失序賣壓則會限制這個空間。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Iran Deal Hopes Drive a Broad Treasury Rally

Treasuries rallied sharply on Thursday after the US president canceled planned strikes and said an agreement with Iran could be announced. Falling oil pushed the expected timing of a fully priced Fed increase from December into the first quarter of 2027. The 10-year yield dropped 10 basis points to 4.45%, with real yields and inflation compensation contributing equally.

Unlike Wednesday's short-lived response to soft core CPI, the relief extended across markets. Semiconductors jumped 7.91%, high-yield bonds gained and volatility fell. Investors were responding to a better prospective growth-inflation balance as energy risk receded, rather than fleeing weak growth. The 30-year Treasury yield returned below 5%, and its reopening drew improved cover with a large direct bid.

The economic and policy news still gave reasons for caution. Producer prices rose more than expected, including beyond energy, while jobless claims edged higher. The ECB raised rates and left room for another increase. In credit, Citi and CoreWeave completed large offerings, but Hanuman Wind Power postponed its debut again despite offering a high yield. Cheaper oil eased the common constraint without eliminating the differences in borrowers' finances or the inflation already moving through supply chains.

## Oil Relief Overcomes Hot Producer Prices

WTI fell 2.58% to $87.71 and Brent dropped 2.92% to $90.38 as expectations for an agreement reduced the war premium. Before the geopolitical news, contracts had fully priced a quarter-point Fed increase by December; by the close, that point had moved into the first quarter of 2027. Inflation risk was being deferred, not replaced by expectations for cuts.

The Treasury rally was broad. The 2-year yield fell 8 basis points to 4.05%, the 5-year declined 9 to 4.18%, and the 30-year dropped 8 to 4.95%. The 2s10s spread narrowed 2 basis points to 40, while 2s30s stayed at 90. The 2s5s10s butterfly held at −14; 2s10s30s fell 4 basis points to −10 as the 10-year led the move.

At ten years, the real yield and breakeven each declined 5 basis points, to 2.16% and 2.29%. Five-year real yields also fell 5 basis points to 1.78%, seven-year yields dropped 6 to 1.96%, and the 20- and 30-year real yields fell 5 and 6 to 2.53% and 2.72%. Lower inflation compensation reflected oil relief; lower real yields accompanied the reduced urgency to tighten.

The rally erased much of the recent rise. The 2- and 5-year yields were unchanged over the week but still 10 and 11 basis points higher over the month. The 10-year was down 2 basis points weekly and up 3 monthly, while the 30-year was down 2 and 3. Policy-sensitive yields nevertheless remained above the Fed's target range.

May PPI was an uncomfortable backdrop. Final-demand prices rose 1.1% monthly against a 0.7% consensus, and 6.5% year on year. Excluding food, energy and trade services, prices increased 0.8% monthly and 5.1% yearly, above the 0.5% monthly estimate. Goods prices jumped 2.8%, led by energy at 10.7%, while services rose 0.3%. The pressure was not confined to crude.

Claims offered a counterweight. Initial applications rose 4,000 to 229,000 in the week ended June 6, above the 220,000 estimate, and the four-week average increased to 219,000. Continuing claims rose 24,000 to 1.795 million in the week ended May 30. The insured unemployment rate held at 1.2%, but more people were entering and remaining on benefits. Alongside cheaper oil, those readings made waiting less costly for the Fed before its June 16–17 meeting.

Risk assets welcomed the same relief. The S&P 500 rose 1.75%, Nasdaq 100 gained 3.29% and semiconductors jumped 7.91%; VIX fell 12.51% to 19.44. The dollar index slipped 0.09% to 99.86 and gold declined 0.44% to $4,090.30. Negotiation headlines have repeatedly changed during the war, however, and the producer-price report showed that earlier energy costs were already spreading.

## Auctions Clear as the Fed Maintains Reserve Support

The $22 billion 30-year reopening cleared at 5.020%, with bid-to-cover improving to 2.33 from 2.30 at the prior, larger sale. Indirect bidders took 59.95%, direct bidders 25.31% and dealers 14.74%. The 5% bond matures in May 2056 and settles June 15. End users absorbed the smaller offering with a substantial direct bid; the result did not interrupt the rally.

Bill demand was more mixed. Treasury accepted $70 billion of four-week bills at a 3.595% high rate, with cover rising to 3.13 from 3.07 and indirect buyers taking 70.59%. The $75.001 billion eight-week sale cleared at 3.610%, with cover falling to 2.94 from 3.20 and indirect participation of 69.59%. Both settle June 16. The shorter sale benefited from a reduced amount, while unchanged eight-week supply drew weaker cover.

Coupon-equivalent yields held at 3.67% for four weeks and 3.68% for six. The eight-week rose 1 basis point to 3.69%; 13-, 17- and 26-week yields each fell 1 basis point to 3.71%, 3.76% and 3.80%. The 52-week declined 5 basis points to 3.85% as expected tightening moved farther out.

The Fed kept planned bill purchases near $10 billion for the monthly period ending July 13 and scheduled about $16.5 billion of reinvestments. Bank reserves rose $65.8 billion to $3.111 trillion in the week through June 10. These reserve-management operations help maintain ample liquidity as Treasury eventually rebuilds its cash balance above $1 trillion, which would otherwise drain bank reserves.

Investors also considered how Chair Kevin Warsh might communicate policy. Pimco advisers noted his earlier criticism of forward guidance, while markets discussed shorter FOMC statements, less emphasis on the dot plot and fewer chair press conferences. None had been adopted. Less guidance could make incoming data more influential and increase event volatility without itself changing rate or balance-sheet policy.

## Credit Rewards Clear Funding Plans, Not Every Borrower

Credit funds rose with Treasuries and equities: LQD gained 0.85%, HYG 0.59% and JNK 0.57%. Citi's operating bank completed its first such offering of the year, a $6.25 billion four-part sale spanning two to six years. Pricing on the longest tranche tightened to 67 basis points over Treasuries from about 95 initially. Expected ratings were Aa3, A+ and AA−, with proceeds for general corporate purposes.

Looser long-term-debt requirements had reduced Citi's urgency to issue. The other five largest Wall Street banks had already sold more than $120 billion during the year, including over $65 billion in a record first quarter. Citi was one of three borrowers bringing more than $10 billion of US high-grade supply on Thursday. Issuance at the operating bank, rather than holding company, added term funding without signaling distressed balance-sheet repair.

Oracle's financing guidance produced a measurable credit response. Its 3.65% note due 2041 tightened 15 basis points to a 2-percentage-point spread by midday; the 6.9% bond due 2052 narrowed 12 basis points to 2.09 percentage points. Five-year CDS fell by as much as 0.034 percentage point to 1.557. Oracle said it did not expect another calendar-year bond sale and planned $40 billion of debt and equity financing for the current fiscal year, including $20 billion of previously announced at-the-market stock issuance.

Investors were rewarding greater funding clarity, not lower investment needs. Annual capital expenditure had reached $55.7 billion against a $50 billion plan, and new-year net spending was expected near $70 billion. Customer prepayments and customer-supplied equipment can reduce immediate cash requirements, but Oracle remains the largest nonfinancial issuer in the US high-grade index with about $117 billion of bonds. Its debt improved even as equity investors questioned returns on the spending.

CoreWeave turned earlier marketing into a completed cross-border sale: €2 billion of six-year notes at 8.5% and $1.25 billion of six-year dollar notes at 9.625%. Euro orders exceeded €7 billion and included most major European high-yield buyers. Ba3/B+/BB− ratings, projected investment near $35 billion and cash burn near $26 billion left a substantial premium for leverage and uncertain profitability despite the strong book.

Landlord financing illustrates how that tenant risk spreads. The previously reported $1.59 billion Applied Digital project sale at 7%, versus 10% for an earlier phase, was still almost 1 percentage point above a recent Amazon-linked project. CoreWeave's five-year protection cost had fallen to 4.52 percentage points from 8.81 in December, helping developers raise more than $8 billion for related projects. The improvement reduced costs across the chain without erasing the distinction from hyperscaler support.

Senator Elizabeth Warren proposed requiring financial firms to report AI debt and equity exposure to the Office of Financial Research. Disclosures would cover chipmakers, data centers, cloud providers and hyperscalers, specifying instruments, amounts, counterparties, rates, terms, collateral and off-balance-sheet debt. The proposal was not law. Separately, SpaceX told IPO investors it had lined up investment-grade ratings from three agencies after a $20 billion financing had lowered its market-implied funding cost. A $75 billion equity raise and expected further bond issuance could turn bridge financing into a much larger high-grade presence.

Oaktree put numbers on the weaker-credit refinancing problem. More than $200 billion of high-yield bonds and leveraged loans traded below 90 cents and above a 15% yield to maturity, much of it associated with 2021–2022 buyouts. Interest added to principal and liability-management transactions had postponed payments and maturities. About one-third of technology borrowers with debt due in 2028 had not demonstrated market access for years and were expected to begin refinancing attempts in the second half, including enterprise-software names in private credit.

The roughly 6.4-percentage-point CCC premium over better-quality junk, a 14-month high reported previously, now had a concrete maturity example. Moody's cut Travelodge deeper into junk; 23% of its €250 million floating-rate notes due 2030 were on loan to short sellers, and short interest in its 2028 bonds was near 7%. It had about £623 million of notes outstanding, including £415 million of secured debt due April 2028. Negative free cash flow and limited deleveraging made refinancing harder despite strength in aggregate high-yield returns.

Hanuman Wind Power failed to secure access. The Energy Absolute subsidiary postponed its international junk-bond debut for a second time after extending orders by a day. A mid-to-high-9% yield did not overcome concern over the Thai parent's governance, past fraud allegations and plans to transfer some proceeds to it. Higher 15-year Treasury rates also weakened the relative value of the proposed 15-year, non-call-five structure. A large yield could not compensate buyers for an unclear governance and cash-flow boundary.

## The ECB Hikes as European Bonds Hold Gains

The ECB raised its deposit rate 25 basis points to 2.25%, its first increase in almost three years and the first major-economy response to the war's inflation shock. Christine Lagarde pointed to energy spreading into indirect costs and expectations. Activity was slowing, particularly in services, but she judged the economy able to absorb tighter policy.

European bonds held gains after the decision, with the 10-year yield down 3 basis points to 3.05%, while the euro stayed near $1.1538. The move had been widely anticipated. ECB projections kept inflation above target into the first half of 2027, and officials did not rule out another increase in July, although September remained the more common expectation. Investors priced two additional moves beyond 2.25%.

The IMF assumed 50 basis points of cumulative tightening in 2026, raised its euro-area inflation forecast to 2.8% from 2.4% and cut growth to 0.9% from 1.1%. Lower oil would help, but officials remained concerned that wages, services and expectations could retain effects of the earlier shock after a peace agreement.

Türkiye formalized the expected pause, holding the one-week repo rate at 37% and the overnight lending rate, now its main funding channel, at 40%. Annual inflation had risen for two months to 32.6%, although seasonally adjusted inflation improved slightly in May, and the bank tightened credit-growth limits. Year-end consensus near 30% remained above its 26% forecast, leaving possible third-quarter easing dependent on disinflation and a stable lira.

Norway's survey favored more patience. Norges Bank projected output growth of 0.2% in the second quarter and 0.3% in the third, below the previous 0.4% second-quarter view. Hiring difficulties and capacity constraints eased, reducing pressure for another June increase despite faster core inflation. Wage expectations rose to 4.5%, while oil revenue supported the krone. The case for holding rested on weaker activity and currency strength, not an absence of price pressure.

Thailand offered a different curve opportunity. Its 2s10s spread was close to 110 basis points, near the steepest since November 2022, and 10-year yields were estimated roughly 40 basis points above fair value. Softer May inflation and weak growth reduced the likelihood of a Bank of Thailand increase over three to six months. Long bonds offered carry and rolldown if inflation stayed contained and supply did not overwhelm demand.

UK investors faced political and fiscal uncertainty ahead of the June 18 Makerfield by-election and Bank of England decision. A possible Labour leadership challenge could alter borrowing plans after April's deficit reached a six-year high for that month. Conventional gilts total about £2.1 trillion, or roughly £2.9 trillion including linkers and bills. National debt is projected at 105.4% of GDP in 2027, versus 98.8% in 2023, leaving the long end sensitive to any change in fiscal direction.

## Easier Global Conditions Leave Indonesia Behind

EMB gained 0.96% as lower Treasury yields, cheaper oil and a slightly softer dollar improved the common backdrop. Indonesia moved the other way. Its 10-year local yield rose 10 basis points to 7.45%, near the highest since 2022, and the rupiah fell 0.2%, leaving it about 7% weaker for the year. Foreign withdrawals reached $597 million from bonds and $3.9 billion from equities. Analysts saw another 25–50 basis points of tightening as the central bank tolerated higher yields to defend the currency.

Danantara nevertheless completed its debut dollar sale. The sovereign wealth fund raised $1.5 billion in equal five- and ten-year tranches, with the five-year yielding 5.35%. Both priced about 35 basis points inside initial talk, but final books were less than twice covered, below the three-times-or-better demand common in recent Asian deals. The fund also continued considering below-market local-currency bonds. Offshore execution met one funding need without resolving local confidence or recent widening in Indonesian dollar spreads.

Argentina's prior-evening upgrade was reflected in bond prices. The 2035 global rose as much as 2.9 cents to a record 79.4, and the 2030 notes gained more than 1.2 cents. S&P's increase to B− from CCC+ followed fiscal surpluses, more than $10 billion of reserve purchases and better external liquidity. Investors saw potential for spreads to narrow toward 400–450 basis points, a range that could reopen international issuance, though the credit remained speculative grade.

Zambia's local debt rally connected improved access rules with external debt management. Domestic bonds had returned 39% in 2026, more than twice the next-best EM, supported by a 120-basis-point yield decline and a 24% kwacha gain. Raising foreign investors' primary-market cap from 5% to 23% attracted inflows, while stronger copper receipts helped. The $1.36 billion dollar-bond repurchase was expected to free about $275 million for the electricity grid. Those changes reinforced local performance without implying that the buyback alone caused it.

Dangote's Nigerian refinery sought up to $1 billion of private debt as it prepared an IPO and expanded a plant central to domestic fuel supply. Meetings were ongoing, not a completed financing. A separate private share placement had attracted up to $2 billion of indicated demand, and the group targeted at least $40 billion of investment over five years. The debt's eventual leverage, collateral and currency terms will determine how much risk sits within the industrial group rather than banks or the state.

Venezuela's proposed advisory mandate showed the costs preceding a restructuring. A draft discussed with Centerview envisaged an uncapped success fee of 0.1% of restructured debt, implying roughly $150 million–$200 million on claims estimated at $150 billion–$200 billion, plus $750,000 monthly and expenses. Work would cover economic analysis, creditor strategy and multilateral coordination. No final contract or debt terms had been agreed, leaving the claim perimeter and professional costs unresolved.

Zimbabwe discussed a $150 million African Development Bank loan within an effort to raise $2.5 billion for arrears clearance. Excluded from international capital markets since 1999, it seeks to restructure about $23 billion of debt. An IMF staff-monitored program and earlier $4 million AfDB grant improved the institutional path, but bridge funds still need to produce creditor normalization before conventional issuance becomes realistic.

Peru held its benchmark at 4.25% for a ninth month as Lima inflation eased to 3.91% from 4.01%, the first monthly moderation since October. Inflation remained above the 1%–3% target after energy, gas and food shocks. A razor-thin presidential count sustained political uncertainty, but the central bank chose to wait for supply pressure to fade rather than increase rates immediately.

## Incoming Data Will Test the Delayed-Hike View

The preliminary Michigan survey arrives June 12 at 10:00 ET, followed by industrial production June 15 at 09:15. Import and export prices and housing starts are due June 16 at 08:30, with retail sales June 17 at 08:30 before the FOMC decision at 14:00. Softer inflation expectations and interest-sensitive activity would support holding the 3.50%–3.75% range without signaling an imminent increase. Renewed price pressure alongside firm demand would challenge the relief before Warsh's first policy communication.

June 15 brings $119 billion of gross coupon settlement and auctions of $89 billion in 13-week and $77 billion in 26-week bills. June 16 follows with $65 billion of six-week bills and a $13 billion 20-year reopening; June 18 brings a $24 billion five-year TIPS reopening. Funding rates, bidder allocations, the 20-year stop against when-issued trading and demand for real yields will show whether balance sheets can accommodate the sequence after Thursday's rally.

The BOJ and RBA decide June 16, followed June 18 by Bank Indonesia, the SNB, Norges Bank, the Bank of England and the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. The BOJ is expected to lift rates toward 1%. Elsewhere, the questions are whether hold decisions retain tightening language and whether Indonesia or the Philippines acts to defend currencies against imported inflation. Lower oil creates more room for divergence; renewed currency weakness or disorderly long-bond selling would limit it.

overall_summary.headline: Iran deal hopes drive a broad Treasury rally
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Canceled US strikes and hopes of an Iran agreement sent WTI down 2.58% and helped the 10-year Treasury yield fall to 4.45%. Real yield and breakeven inflation each declined 5 basis points. Contracts shifted a fully priced quarter-point Fed increase from December into the first quarter of 2027.

May PPI rose 1.1% monthly and its broader exclusion measure gained 0.8%, while initial claims increased to 229,000. The inflation-labor tension remained, but lower energy risk supported both bonds and equities: semiconductors jumped 7.91%. The 30-year auction cleared with improved cover, and the Fed maintained reserve-management purchases.

Citi and CoreWeave completed large sales. Oracle bonds and CDS improved on clearer financing guidance, whereas Hanuman Wind Power postponed its debut again. The ECB raised rates to 2.25%; Indonesia's local market deteriorated despite a completed Danantara dollar sale. Incoming US data and next week's central-bank decisions will test whether oil relief can sustain the delayed-hike view.
overall_summary.summary: The 10-year yield fell 10 basis points as real yields and breakevens each dropped 5. Oil relief outweighed hot PPI, stocks surged and the expected hike moved later, though the ECB tightened and weaker borrowers still struggled.

watch_events.market_implication: That supports waiting; renewed price pressure and firm demand challenge the delayed-hike view.
